sentences.text: Cobelodus was a predator reaching lengths of 1.5 to 2 meters, distinguished by unusual 30 cm long, flexible cartilaginous tentacles sprouting from its pectoral fins.
The specific purpose of these tentacles remains unknown to scientists.
The type specimen, originally assigned to the genus Styptobasis, was discovered by Edward Drinker Cope in the Illinois Basin black coal shales.
Rainer Zangerl reassigned the species S. aculeata to the genus Cobelodus in 1973.
This animal fed on mollusks, octopuses, and crustaceans.
Cobelodus is classified in the extinct order Symmoriida, with its parent group being the family Symmoriidae.
The animal lived from the late Carboniferous to the early Permian period, specifically between the Visean and Artinskian stages, from 335.4 to 283.3 million years ago.
